PASSO 1: lembre do português: «espero qu: STEP 1: think of English sentences like "I hope you've arrived safely", "I doubt he's finished", "I'm glad you came". The finished action after the trigger is, in Spanish, the pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo. STEP 2: you form it with the present subjunctive of «haber» + participle: «haya llegado». It's the «he llegado» you know, with the auxiliary switched to the subjunctive. STEP 3: the present subjunctive of «haber»: haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan. Only «hayáis» has an accent. STEP 4: the participle is the usual one (hablado, comido, vivido; hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto, vuelto, roto…) and never changes for gender or number. STEP 5: this tense comes after the same triggers you've already seen (wishing, doubt, emotion, judgement), but now the action is finished: «Me alegra que hayas venido» (I'm glad you came — you came, and I'm glad about it). Note: English often uses the simple past here ("I'm glad you CAME"); Spanish uses «hayas venido». STEP 6: compare with the present subjunctive: «Me alegra que vengas» (I'm glad you're coming) × «Me alegra que hayas venido» (I'm glad you came). STEP 7: the logic follows the indicative. «Creo que ha llegado» (indicative) becomes «No creo que haya llegado» (subjunctive) — English "I think he's arrived" / "I don't think he's arrived". «Sé que lo ha visto» becomes «Dudo que lo haya visto». STEP 8: negation and pronouns go before «haya»: «No creo que lo haya visto», «Es posible que se haya olvidado» (he may have forgotten). STEP 9: careful: «haya» is not «hay». «Hay» is "there is"; «haya» is the subjunctive, as in «Es posible que haya problemas» (there may be problems).

PASSO 1: a pergunta-chave é: a ação já t: STEP 1: the key question: is the action finished, or is it still to come (or happening now)? STEP 2: if it's happening now, habitual or still to come, use the present subjunctive: «Espero que llegues bien» (I hope you get there safely — said before the trip). STEP 3: if it's finished, use the pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo: «Espero que hayas llegado bien» (I hope you got there safely — you've already arrived). STEP 4: the same trigger changes meaning with the tense: «Me alegra que vengas» (I'm glad you're coming) and «Me alegra que hayas venido» (I'm glad you came). STEP 5: «dudo, no creo, es posible, puede que» follow the same rule: «Dudo que venga» (I doubt he'll come) and «Dudo que haya venido» (I doubt he came). STEP 6: use the perfecto for any finished fact, today's or yesterday's, when the trigger is in the present: «No creo que lo haya dicho ayer» (I don't think he said it yesterday). In lesson 46 you'll see the other option, with the imperfecto de subjuntivo. STEP 7: with «ojalá», the perfecto wishes for something that has already happened but that you don't know about: «Ojalá haya dormido bien» (I hope he slept well). STEP 8: useful fixed phrases: «que yo sepa» (as far as I know) and «que yo recuerde» (as far as I remember).

PASSO 1: no futuro, as orações de tempo: STEP 1: about the future, time clauses take the subjunctive (lesson 44): «cuando llegues, llámame». STEP 2: when you want to make clear that the first action FINISHES before the second, use «haya» + participle: «Llámame cuando hayas terminado» (Call me when you've finished). STEP 3: English does the same with its present perfect: "when you've finished", "as soon as I've arrived", "after they've left". The trap: English "when you HAVE finished" uses the indicative «has», but Spanish needs the subjunctive «hayas». STEP 4: the conjunctions are the same as before: «cuando, en cuanto, tan pronto como, después de que, una vez que, hasta que». STEP 5: the difference in meaning is small. «Cuando termines, llámame» is natural ("when you finish"). «Cuando hayas terminado, llámame» stresses that the action must be complete. STEP 6: with «después de que» and «una vez que», the perfecto is very common: «Una vez que hayas pagado, recibirás el billete» (Once you've paid, you'll receive the ticket). STEP 7: the main clause is in the future, the imperative or the present with a future meaning. STEP 8: typical mistakes are the future and «he» + participle after «cuando», which don't work here.
